7192295b7a20.title: Research Engineer / Scientist, Data & Evals
7192295b7a20.description: WHY HARVEY At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come. This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched. Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you. At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started. ROLE OVERVIEW In this role, you'll build the data and measurement systems that power our post-training, benchmarking, and agent capability efforts. We recently post-trained our first model built for legal work, and we’re now building the team to scale up our post-training efforts. You’ll own synthetic data pipelines, evaluation design, the tasks and grading behind training environments, and the systems that turn feedback from domain experts into training signals and rewards. These are tasks where correctness often can’t be verified automatically, so defining and measuring quality is a core research challenge. You’ll join a small, high-bar team of hands-on engineers and researchers, where each person owns a large part of the work. We’re looking for research engineers who can build reliable data and evaluation systems, question what a metric actually tells us, and work closely with researchers and legal experts to turn model failures into measurable improvements. Learn more about our work at harvey.ai/research http://harvey.ai/research. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Build synthetic data pipelines that generate, filter, and curate training and evaluation samples for complex legal reasoning and agentic workflows. - Design evaluations and verifiers that reflect real legal work, calibrate them against expert judgment, and investigate where they fail. - Build and maintain capability benchmarks like our Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB), along with product-focused evals that track how models perform on real customer workflows. - Work with legal domain experts to define quality metrics, rubrics, and other grading mechanisms for training and evaluation. - Own training and evaluation data quality, including provenance, coverage, and safeguards against contamination. - Close the loop from prod

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara’s Machine Learning, AI, Analytics & Data (MAAD) team builds the intelligence and technology that helps our go-to-market teams work faster, make better decisions, and spend more time with customers.

As the Director, GTM AI Engineering you’ll run our AI Engineering team for GTM. You’ll work closely with Data Science, Analytics, and Data Engineering to serve Sales, Customer Success, Support, Enablement, and GTM leadership. This is a hands-on Director role. Expect to spend about 70% of your time building (prototyping agents, writing code, designing evals) and about 30% leading the team, setting strategy, and influencing stakeholders.

You’ll build intelligent workflow experiences. That ranges from AI agents and copilots that take manual work off sellers’ plates, to signals for propensity and prioritization, to the data, evaluation, and measurement foundations that make these products reliable and trusted.

The ideal candidate is AI-native. You already run your own work through agents every day, you’ve shipped AI products to production, and you get as excited about a seller’s first “wow, this saved me an hour” moment as you do about a clean architecture.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US.

In this role, you will:

  • Build hands-on. Prototype, ship, and iterate on AI agents, copilots, and workflow automations for GTM teams, from the first demo to a production system people rely on.
  • Build the platform, not just the apps. Own the architecture of the shared GTM

Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About this role:

Samsara’s cloud-connected sensor platform collects observations about the world in near real-time. Samsara builds an extensive set of products, including battery-powered, wireless sensors, Linux-based IoT gateways, and Internet-connected dashcams. These devices are the building blocks Samsara uses to construct enterprise solutions for a wide range of verticals, including commercial fleet management and industrial monitoring. Through a unique integration of sensor data such as GPS, acceleration, temperature, video, and more, we enable our customers to gain greater insights into operations, identify and eliminate inefficiencies, and react to alerts all in near real-time.

As a Firmware Engineer at Samsara, you will develop software that runs on millions of devices, deployed by our industrial and enterprise customers. You’ll tackle challenges including evaluating and selecting hardware components, bringing up new hardware platforms and sensors, building systems to gather data and detect meaningful events, and structuring recorded data to allow efficient analysis across thousands of devices while providing deep insights into individual events.

We use C for our MCU-based platforms, Golang for embedded applications on Linux-based gateways and backend services, Google protocol buffers to structure data, and various AWS technologies to process and store data. Experience with these exact technologies is not required.

Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact

This isn't a relationship management role. It's an ownership role. Sharp. Adaptable. Unstoppable. As a Mission Engineer II, you'll work directly alongside public safety agencies to turn real operational challenges into working technical solutions.

You'll spend time with the people doing the work, understand how the agency operates, identify problems worth solving, and use Axon tools, AI, automation, data, and the broader Axon ecosystem to build against them. 

Building is the core of the role, but customer needs come first. Because you're embedded with the agency, you'll also become a go-to technical resource who understands their Axon environment and helps them navigate critical needs when they arise. You may help quarterback an upcoming deployment, coordinate a complex technical issue, or connect the right Axon teams around an agency priority.

You won't replace Support, Deployment, Product, or other teams. You'll bring technical continuity, help connect the dots, and use what you learn to identify the next opportunity to build something better. Mission Engineers don't measure success by activity. They measure it by what gets built, what gets used, and what changes because of it.

What You’ll Do

Location: On Site with travel
Reports To: Manager or Senior Manager of Mission Engineering

Discover the Mission

  • Embed with assigned agencies to understand their mission, people, workflows, systems, and priorities.
  • Develop broad knowledge of the Axon ecosystem and deeper expertise in the products deployed at your agency.
  • Work with frontline users, technical teams, and agency leadership to uncover operational friction.
  • Translate customer problems into clear technical requirements and measurable success criteria.
  • Identify opportunities for AI, automation, data, and Axon capabilities to improve how the agency operates.
  • Understand what the customer needs—not simply what they initially ask for.

Build With the Platform

  • Build applications, dashboards, workflows, automations, and using Axon products and other approved Axon tools.
  • Apply foundational software engineering concepts including APIs, data structures, scripting, testing, debugging

83d4007e9271.description: SENIOR SECURITY ENGINEER LiteLLM is the world’s most popular AI Gateway, trusted by companies like Adobe, Netflix, and NASA. Our platform gives developers secure, reliable access to LLMs and adjacent services. We’re looking for our first Security Engineer to help secure LiteLLM’s application, infrastructure, and software-delivery pipeline. ABOUT THE ROLE This is a hands-on security generalist role with a strong emphasis on application security. You’ll spend most of your time reviewing and hardening LiteLLM’s Python codebase, identifying new attack surfaces, working directly with engineers to fix vulnerabilities, and making secure development practices part of how we build. You’ll also own security work across IT, CI/CD, cloud infrastructure, and the software supply chain. The ideal candidate has built application/product/infrastructure security programs from scratch and genuinely enjoys security outside of work—through CTFs, vulnerability research, open-source projects, or independent experimentation. RESPONSIBILITIES APPLICATION SECURITY - Conduct deep security reviews of LiteLLM’s Python proxy, APIs, authentication systems, and enterprise features. - Identify and remediate vulnerabilities involving authentication, authorization, secrets, tenant isolation, injection, and data exposure. - Partner directly with engineers throughout design, implementation, code review, and release—not only after code is shipped. - Build application-security tooling into the development lifecycle, including SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, and secrets detection. - Perform internal red teaming and adversarial testing against LiteLLM’s APIs, proxy, and LLM-specific attack surfaces. - Threat-model new products and architecture changes before they reach production. - Create secure coding guidelines and train engineers on common vulnerabilities and defensive practices. INFRASTRUCTURE, CI/CD, AND SUPPLY-CHAIN SECURITY - Harden LiteLLM’s Docker images, PyPI packages, GitHub Actions workflows, and release infrastructure. - Detect dependency confusion, poisoned packages, compromised dependencies, exposed secrets, and unsafe build practices. - Implement SBOMs, signed builds, provenance checks, and reproducible-build practices. - Design secure-by-default configurations for cloud and self-hosted deployments, including authentication, IAM, secrets management, and key rotation. - Review cloud infrastructure, network boundaries, access controls, and production deployment patterns. IT SECURITY AND INCIDENT RESPONSE - Strengthen employee identity, device, SaaS, and internal access controls. - Build monitoring and anomaly detection for suspicious API, model, authentication, and routing activity. - Lead security incident response, vulnerability assessment, remediation, post-mortems, and stakeholder communication. - Establish formal vulnerability intake, CVE triage, disclosure, and remediation processes. - Maintain threat models as LiteLLM’s product and architecture evolve. About Epic

Epic Kids is the leading digital reading platform built for kids 12 and under, trusted by millions of children, educators, and families around the world. Our mission is to inspire a lifelong love of reading by providing unlimited access to thousands of high-quality books, videos, and educational content through a safe and engaging experience. At Epic, you'll join a collaborative and fast-paced global team passionate about building meaningful products that make a real impact on children's education and literacy.

You'll own Epic's native Android app, the main way kids open a book on Android phones, tablets and Chromebooks. It's a large, mature Kotlin codebase with some Java and xml UI layouts.   • Testing with JUnit, Mockito or MockK, Robolectric and Espresso.

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

It is not usable at institutional scale. Despite being open, blockchain data is fragmented, hard to interpret, and painful to maintain. Even a simple question like “Who are the largest Ethereum token holders over time?” can require running nodes, ingesting full chain history, decoding contracts, cleaning edge cases, and writing complex SQL. BLOCKCHAINS ARE OPTIMIZED FOR WRITES, NOT READS. They are built for consensus and execution, not searchability, standardization, or financial interpretation. Blockchains are computers, not databases https://x.com/Tim_Roughgarden/status/1512847113599729668. Every protocol defines its own schema. The same economic action can be encoded in dozens of different ways. The result: - Fragmented standards - Exponential complexity - No accountability for interpretation - Events without economic meaning Finance cannot operate on that, it needs an effective system of record. ALLIUM IS BUILDING THE SYSTEM OF RECORD FOR ONCHAIN FINANCE Allium ingests, verifies, and standardizes data across 140+ blockchains and 30+ petabytes of history. We close four structural gaps that prevent blockchains from becoming systems of record: - Semantic Gap: Translating raw events into financial concepts like payments, trades, deposits, and staking income - Standardization Gap: Mapping thousands of protocols into a single canonical cross chain schema - Infrastructure Gap: Read optimized, globally distributed data at web scale - Accountability Gap: Auditable methodology, SLAs, and SOC 1 and 2 compliance The result is a neutral, canonical data layer institutions can build on with confidence. FINANCE IS MOVING ONCHAIN Stablecoins, tokenized assets, trading, staking, and lending are growing rapidly. Institutions need a trusted source of truth for onchain financial activity, just as they rely on Bloomberg or DTCC in traditional markets. Raw blockchains cannot serve that role. As AI agents begin transacting autonomously https://x.com/AlliumLabs/status/2019810793324482901?s=20, the requirement becomes even stricter. Agents cannot reason over raw event logs. They need structured data, attribution, condition checks, and auditability. Allium is the read layer that makes onchain finance usable for humans and machines. WHO WE SERVE Allium powers three core personas with the same canonical data foundation: 1. Finance, Accounting, and Risk Teams They need reliable, audit grade answers. They rely on Allium for financial reporting, reconciliation, compliance, risk monitoring, and defensible metrics that can stand up to auditors and regulators. 2. This role leads teams embedded within the Customer Identity product unit and works across multiple functions to deliver proactive threat intelligence, get ahead of emerging attack vectors, and build the security software that protects our platform, supporting the growth of our global Customer Identity business.

We are an engineering-focused organization that seeks to stay on the cutting edge of security technology and the threat landscape. An overview of this role

As a Software Engineer on GitLab's Authorization team, you'll help build and maintain the system that decides what every user, token, and automated agent can access on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated. You'll work alongside experienced engineers who guide the larger design decisions, delivering well-scoped changes and growing into ownership of larger parts of the system.

Today, that work is Ruby on Rails. Roughly 400 policy classes and a catalog of about 1,900 permissions sit behind every application programming interface (API) request. You'll work on fine-grained token permissions, custom roles, and the GraphQL and representational state transfer (REST) APIs that enforce them. A single request can trigger hundreds of permission checks, so correctness and performance both matter.

You'll also contribute to moving the permission model to a new authorization stack that pairs the Rails monolith with a Rust policy engine. The engine represents access relationships and evaluates permission rules, and can run within the monolith's process or be reached through remote procedure calls using gRPC. You don't need prior Rust experience: several engineers on the team learned it for this work, and we'll support you doing the same.

Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake.

The role in a nutshell:

We're looking for a Security Engineer to support fellow engineers across three critical functional areas: Identity and Access Management (IAM), AI, and Cloud. This is an earlier-career role built for someone with a strong IT administration and/or software development foundation who's ready to grow into security — you don't need deep expertise across all three areas, but you should bring real, hands-on experience in at least one, along with the technical fundamentals to ramp quickly into the others. HA/DR for our control infrastructure, a declarative model for the whole platform, and a deployment control plane, all designed while a live platform keeps running. - Everything sits on top of it. It is philanthropically funded and built by a small team across North America, Europe and India, together with the labs who pilot the tools with us. WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING You'll join a small and friendly distributed team of engineers, designers and researchers who are designing, building and testing new ways of doing collaborative science. We do most of our work in writing, across many time zones, and there are no managers: engineers pull their own work from a shared queue, and we judge progress by what researchers do with the tools. You'll put early versions in front of researchers, and their interest will settle which ones grow. You'll also help make the plugins far easier to start with, so that a new user gets something useful back within minutes of installing one. You'll work closely with our designer and with a product manager we are hiring at the same time, who keeps one ordered queue of work with the team. You'll turn the most promising ideas on it into prototypes people can try, and carry the ones that earn their place through to something the team can maintain. Technical choices that are cheap to reverse are yours to make, and you'll talk the expensive ones through with our tech lead. We write TypeScript, with a Supabase (Postgres) database, an MCP server and a canvas built on tldraw. a47f5b9b5805.description: ABOUT STANDARD BOTS Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next. ABOUT THE ROLE *We're hiring a Lead, but if you're a strong functional safety engineer at Senior, Staff or Principal level, we still want to hear from you. We'll level the role and the offer to the person. If you want a mature process to run, this isn't the role. If you want to build the safety organization behind the best cobot in the world, with the authority to do it, read on. Standard Bots arms work right next to people, installed by customers who may have never set up a robot before, with no cage and no integrator's risk assessment to lean on. The robot has to be safe by design, and you'll be the one who proves it. We want to build the best collaborative robot in the world, and that's impossible without building the safest one: a robot anyone can put next to their people on day one and trust. Most of the industry treats safety as paperwork at the end. We want it to be the thing our robots are known for — designed in from the first sketch and proven on real hardware. Until now, safety has lived inside our hardware, firmware and test teams, like it does at most young companies that ship. That got our first robots out the door. It won't carry what's next: volume growing fast, several new products in development, and AI changing how robots are taught. So we're pulling safety into one strong team with its own mandate — and that team needs a leader. 📍 LOCATION Remote within the US or Europe, with regular on-site time at our factory in Glen Cove, NY. Requires approximately one week a month onsite, more during validation rounds and assessor visits, since the verification work happens on real robots. Weekly on site is a plus, not a condition. WHAT YOU'LL OWN - The safety case. You own it across our products — analysis, architecture, and the certification plan that gets each robot through third-party assessment. - The relationship with assessors. You're our technical voice toward notified bodies and NRTLs, and you're the one in the room defending the argument. - Verification on real robots. Every safety function gets tested on hardware you trust, fault injection included. You stay hands-on — this is not a reviewing job. - The team. You hire and lead the functional safety engineers who join after you, starting with one who leans electronics and controls and one who leans software. - Safety in the design, not at the gate. You report to the Head of System

Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake.

Chainguard is venture-backed by leading investors, including Amplify, IVP, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis VC, Redpoint Ventures, Sequoia Capital, and Spark Capital.

The role, in a nutshell

Chainguard Containers is our core product, and this team builds it. As a Senior Software Engineer in Container Product Engineering you will design and ship the features, services, and build systems behind Chainguard Containers, working in a small sub-team of two to four engineers that owns one project end to end.

Chainguard is growing explosively. Every line of code is now written with AI in the loop, which means the foundation it runs on has to be secure by default. You will build that foundation: the hardened container images, the registry that serves them, and the tooling that lets engineers and AI agents adopt them.

This is a product role. You will work directly with Product Managers and customers, make the trade-off calls on the features you own, and ship them.

What the team owns

  • Product features for Chainguard Containers. Letting customers push their own images to our registry, Custom Assembly (customers compose images from our hardened packages), Helm charts, notifications, and compliance views such as STIG dashboards (STIG is the US government's hardening standard).
  • The image build pipeline. The systems that turn packages from Wolfi, our Linux distribution, into signed and attested container images at scale, including moving image builds onto our own runner infrastructure.
  • Registry performance and distribution. Work such as lazy loading, so a container starts before its whole image has downloaded, and image signing with Sigstore.
  • Adoption tooling for engineers and AI agents. Migration tools that convert existing Dockerfiles to Chainguard Containers, and MCP servers (Model Context Protocol, the standard that lets AI agents call tools) so agents can discover and pull our images directly.

What you'll do

  • Design, build, and ship new features and services for Chainguard Containers, from a one-page design through production and the first week of customer use.
  • Own the trade-offs on your work: scope, sequencing, what to cut, and when "good enough to ship" beats "complete". Say so clearly when a plan is at risk.
  • Work with AI

Impinj delivers the Physical Intelligence that connects the physical world to the AI-powered digital world, fueling automated workflows and improving consumer experiences. From retail merchandise and groceries to packages and shipping pallets, Impinj products and solutions identify and track tens of billions of everyday items, providing real-time operational insights about every item enterprises make, move and sell. Team Overview:

The Layout Design Engineering group is an integral part of the Silicon Engineering department, working closely with the analog RFID end-point IC development team and the Reader IC team, internationally. The team is responsible for delivering tape-outs for RFID products, test chips, reader ICs, and DOEs (design of experiments) work that sits at the center of how Impinj brings new silicon to market.

Layout decisions made by this team directly influence the power efficiency, cost, and time-to-market of every piece of silicon we ship, making the group's work foundational to Impinj's mission. The team operates with a continuous-improvement mindset, adapting quickly and challenging each other to remain best-in-class in both quality and speed, with meticulous attention to detail to ensure designs have long-term reliability and zero defects, at production volumes in the many billions and eventually trillions of tags per year.

  • Perform detailed transistor-level layout of RF, mixed-signal, and analog circuit blocks for both high-performance RF as well as ultra-low power and compact RFID
  • Work closely with the analog and digital design teams on floor planning, pin placement, power supply strategy and signal distribution between blocks
  • Conduct layout reviews for power/ground routing, electromigration, matching, and signal coupling
  • Participate in schedule meetings coordinating layout and floorplan activities

ced5323d692d.title: Staff Software Engineer, Chainguard Harness
ced5323d692d.description:
Chainguard is the trusted source for open source. By delivering hardened, secure, and production-ready builds of all the open source software engineers and AI agents rely on, Chainguard helps organizations build faster, stay compliant, and eliminate risk. 

Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake.

Chainguard is venture-backed by leading investors, including Amplify, IVP, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis VC, Redpoint Ventures, Sequoia Capital, and Spark Capital.

The role, in a nutshell

At Chainguard we're focused on securing the software supply chain, and we're building the next generation of products at the intersection of security and AI. You'll join a small, fast-moving team building Chainguard Harness.

Chainguard Harness uses frontier AI models to hunt down exploitable vulnerabilities in a customer's application, then delivers validated findings with recommended fixes, with no model access required. Customers trust us with their source code, so security isn't just a feature of this product. It is the product.

As a Staff engineer you'll own large parts of the Harness architecture, guide technical decisions across the team, and help take the product from beta to a service that scales to many more customers and environments.

What you'll do

  • Own major parts of the system end to end, from design through implementation, rollout, and operation

  • Build security into the foundation: protecting customer code end to end, least-privilege access, and auditing everything the system and its operators do. Partner with Product and Security on threat models and reviews.

  • Make Harness a reliable, observable, production-grade service, making sound long-term tradeoffs around scale, cost, technical debt, and build versus buy.

  • Work directly with customers, Product, and our field team. You'll join customer calls and turn feedback into the roadmap.

  • Raise the bar for the team through design docs, code review, and mentoring, and by showing how AI tooling can make a small team move fast without cutting corners on security.

What we're looking for

  • 10+ years of experience in software development

  • A track record of building and operating production services where security and data confidentiality were hard requirements, not afterthoughts

  • Experience designing systems that hold confidential customer data end to end

  • Experience shipping software into air-gapped, disconnected, or highly restricted environments

  • Deep experience with cloud infrastructure on GCP and/or AWS

Participate in incident post-mortems and customer issue reviews — identify gaps in test coverage that allowed a bug to reach production and close them. Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy.

Our team, across some 100 countries, is dedicated to transforming the practice of medicine by working to turn the impossible into the possible. 142a4c52c8b9.description: Builds Operations (AI Ops) Solutions for specific domains. Automates and optimizes IT operations processes, managing risk, incident management, and root cause analysis using artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) techniques. AI Ops aim to reduce the time and effort needed for IT processes while increasing the precision and speed of problem-solving through optimizing the end-to-end lifecycle of artificial intelligence (AI) applications and systems. Collaborates with cross-functional teams, including data scientists, SWEs, and infrastructure/operations, to ensure the reliability, scalability, and performance of IT applications. Automates routine tasks and implements continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines to optimize AI Ops processes and workflows. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint. Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere. We are Cisco, and our power starts with you. 49bfb58db245.description: At Gilead, we’re creating a healthier world for all people. For more than 35 years, we’ve tackled diseases such as HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer – working relentlessly to develop therapies that help improve lives and to ensure access to these therapies across the globe. We continue to fight against the world’s biggest health challenges, and our mission requires collaboration, determination and a relentless drive to make a difference. Every member of Gilead’s team plays a critical role in the discovery and development of life-changing scientific innovations. Our employees are our greatest asset as we work to achieve our bold ambitions, and we’re looking for the next wave of passionate and ambitious people ready to make a direct impact. We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfill their aspirations. Join Gilead and help create possible, together. Job Description Lead the hands-on development of full-stack applications integrated with AI/ML and GenAI capabilities for global pharma and enterprise use cases. Design, build, and maintain scalable front-end, back-end, API, and AI-enabled application components across cloud-native platforms Collaborate with product, engineering, data science, and business teams to deliver intuitive, high-performance digital solutions Develop and integrate AI/ML models, LLM-based services, and intelligent workflows into enterprise applications. Collaborate to drive best practices in software engineering, testing, code quality, security, and performance optimization, adopt where applicable Support CI/CD automation, production deployments, monitoring, and issue resolution in partnership with DevOps teams Mentor junior engineers and contribute to continuous improvement in engineering standards and agile delivery practices. 4+ years of experience in full-stack or AI-focused software engineering roles with Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering or related field, 2+ years with Master’s degree. Proficiency in modern front-end frameworks, back-end technologies, APIs, databases, and cloud-native application development Expertise in integrating AI/ML or GenAI capabilities into enterprise applications Strong understanding of scalable application architecture, microservices, and secure coding practices Experience with cloud platforms, containers, CI/CD pipelines, and agile development methodologies Strong problem-solving, debugging, and collaboration skills within global teams Experience in pharmaceuticals, healthcare, or regulated industries preferred Familiarity with LLM orchestration frameworks, vector databases, and AI application architectures Exposure to MLOps, observability, and AI model deployment practices would be a plus Experienc

4755f50b6add.title: Infrastructure Design Engineer (AVP)
4755f50b6add.description: Job Description Purpose of the role To build and maintain infrastructure platforms and products that support applications and data systems, using hardware, software, networks, and cloud computing platforms as required with the aim of ensuring that the infrastructure is reliable, scalable, and secure. Ensure the reliability, availability, and scalability of the systems, platforms, and technology through the application of software engineering techniques, automation, and best practices in incident response. Accountabilities Build Engineering: Development, delivery, and maintenance of high-quality infrastructure solutions to fulfil business requirements ensuring measurable reliability, performance, availability, and ease of use. Including the identification of the appropriate technologies and solutions to meet business, optimisation, and resourcing requirements. Incident Management: Monitoring of IT infrastructure and system performance to measure, identify, address, and resolve any potential issues, vulnerabilities, or outages. Use of data to drive down mean time to resolution. Automation: Development and implementation of automated tasks and processes to improve efficiency and reduce manual intervention, utilising software scripting/coding disciplines. Security: Implementation of a secure configuration and measures to protect infrastructure against cyber-attacks, vulnerabilities, and other security threats, including protection of hardware, software, and data from unauthorised access. You will apply strong Python and Structured Query Language (SQL) skills and work with Snowflake and modern data engineering technologies to deliver solutions from requirements and technical design through implementation, deployment, and production support. Your work will improve the quality, observability, reliability, and maintainability of production data products while simplifying how new datasets are onboarded and processed.
